what: Adds up all vertical scroll distance (either direction) and maps 1500px to 4500px onto a 0→1 intensity written to html as --fx-chaos, and once it passes .9 puts a chaos marker (is-chaos) on body. At 1 it locks and no longer goes up or down, and when the page is more than half a screen down, the X button (80px, 70px on phones) circles the screen edge clockwise at 2px per frame (1px on phones) — hovering stops it. Pressing the button sinks the intensity to 0 in 1s power2.inOut and the cumulative distance starts building again from 0

options.from: Cumulative scroll (px) at which intensity starts rising, default 1500
options.to: Cumulative scroll (px) at which Century 1 begins, default 4500
options.on: Strength of the body marker, default .9
options.dur: Duration for the button to sink when pressed (seconds), default 1. 0 means immediately
options.size: Button size (px), default 80 (70 at 950px and below)
options.speed: Button spin speed (px per frame at 60fps), default 2 (1 at 950px or below)
options.class: Marker class name added to body, default is-chaos

use: <button type="button" aria-label="Turn Off Chaos" data-fx="scroll-chaos-mode" data-fx-scroll-chaos-mode="from: 1500; to: 4500"><svg viewBox="0 0 64 64">…X…</svg></button>
note: Intensity is output only as the html inline style --fx-chaos — slice-spread-glitch and char-glitch-medley read it, and the site css flips the skin with body.is-chaos (transparent background, mix-blend difference, etc.). The button is placed with position: fixed so it never leaves the screen. With reduce, intensity is 0 and the button is hidden.

from.where: index.html .kk-switch (chaos mode — cumulative scroll 1500→4500, an X button circling the edge)
